commit.message:
Bugfix Five Virtues and adjust description

Staves skill was requiring the next integer level rather than just being
highest. The virtueSH description was also a bit unwieldy, so I have
adjusted it with some assistance from PleasingFungus.

Don't put random tags in the vaults cache

These random rolls were being made at validation time as well as
generation time. This meant that on any particular build, the
validation-rolled tags would be present for all instances of a vault,
even those with a different seed. This gave unintended tags, and in the
case of the vaults vault affected seed stability across different builds
which rolled different tags.

Don't limit ghosts/illusions to primary weapons.

Ghost demon overrides assume only one weapon. So give dual-wielding
player ghosts/player illusions a 50/50 chance of getting their offhand
weapon (if they're wielding one) instead of their primary weapon.

Closes #5518.

Remove summoning caps except for Summon Holies.

Since it needs them, and having such caps on the other spells has
unintended side effects on monster positioning.

This partially reverts a780400260f2cd0ff759cd51bbc026d0ca0630fb.

Consistently count bands for shadow creatures cap

There are two ways in which summon caps are used:
first, to stop monsters from trying to cast a spell if it's capped,
second, to expire old monsters if summons exceed the cap.

Until now, shadow creatures has been exceptional in that these two
counts were inconsistent, because shadow creatures can spawn bands,
and the latter use case counted every band as a single monster,
while the former use case counted every monster individually.

Unify these two approaches consistently by always counting
shadow creatures' summoned bands as a single monster towards the cap.
Add monspell entries for the strange machine

Address message spam from overeager summoners

For spells that create multiple summons in a single cast,
monsters will attempt to cast them even if they're only at one less
than the summon cap, which causes excessive work and message spam
from creating more monsters than necessary and then dismissing
enough monsters to make room for the newly-created ones.

Instead, when monsters attempt to cast summons, limit the number of
summons they can create to only the number of available summon slots.

The only effect on gameplay is that the average age of summons on the field
will increase (because summons aren't being prematurely dismissed),
but IME it's uncommon for a single fight to last long enough in the first
place for summons to time out naturally, and if it did turn out to be
a problem then it would be trivial to bump summon durations upward.

Refactor logic for dismissing oldest summons

I found this function, formerly named `summoned_monster`, to be confusingly
named and somewhat difficult to understand.
I've refactored it to hopefully be more readable, adding documentation
where helpful.
This should result in no logical changes compared to the previous rendition.

Fix thy/thine agreement in insults.

This requires adding thy/thine to all possible parts, as well as
slightly rewording one message since said parts are not capitalised.
Fix thy/thine agreement.

Add another weapon name to artefacts.

(From the Schlock Mercenary warship.)
Add another apocalyptic name to artefact weapons.

Delete 'Fimbulwinter' from rand_wpn.txt

Removed 'Fimbulwinter' from the random weapon list.

Add a function to check a player's primary form since a given XL

Intended mostly to be used for titles, player_exclusively_used_form_since()
checks whether the player's current base form was the only form they gained
any XP in, start from a given XL.

This is quite a bit more heavyweight than other things we check when
redrawing titles, but even scanning ~600 or so array entries each redraw is
surely not relevant in practice.

Track flux form in the form XP table

The form XP table normally only considers the player's base form at the
time they gain XP (to avoid messing up the numbers due to hostile polymorph
or !lig), but flux is in a unique state where it's technically temporary,
but much *less* temporary. And so, I think it should be tracked as if it
were the primary form the player was in when they fight that way.

Fix description of earthen dragon vein.

It only attacks 2 enemies, not 3.

Closes #5487.
Rewrap a mutation description.
Fix a changed spellbook name in vaults
Improve Revenant ability description

Adjust a spellbook name (powerbf, Predelnik).

Since "sojourn in" is proper wording, as opposed to "sojourn through."
And since the book's description mentions travelling, pluralise it as
"sojourns in."

Also update the corresponding comment and enum name.

Closes #5505.
Fix typo and tweak wording

This logic was accidentally broken by ee4e0f2 which changed the semantics
of this function in a way that made the neutral check unreachable most of
the time.

(Most of the negative effects of this were seperately fixed by bc8265e, but
non-Ely worshippers should still not be forced to attack neutrals if they
don't want to.)

items.shopping_list() and items.shop_inventory() were both stated to

Committer's note: very minor style changes

Reword glimmer cloud description a bit (powerbf).

Closes #5508.

"Bound" artefacts -> "corded" ones (Flugkiller).

Randarts which are described as "bound" get miscoloured red since
"bound" is now also used to describe Ash-cursed items. To avoid the
problem, the randart adjective is changed to "corded".

[Committer's note: Adjusted commit message.]

docs: mention the default value of `monster_alert`

Document the default value of an option introduced in 03cf731.
Also, bring back "action" removed by the same commit.

Fix c_answer_prompt overflowing the c++ stack

`yesno` calls `c_answer_prompt` in the player's RC file (if their RC
file contains it). This means that if the player calls `yesno` from
their `c_answer_prompt` function they can overflow the c++ stack.

To fix this, don't allow `c_answer_prompt` to be called recursively from
`yesno`.

Make out of bounds spaces uninhabitable

This fixes a couple of ways jade crystals could end up in them (after
swaps with the player or returning from afar)

Improve how LoS changes interact with exclusions

The range of LoS-sized exclusions now automatically adjusts to account not
just for species, but also form and equipment. In other words, putting on
a scarf of shadows will shrink current and future exclusions, and taking it
off again will expand them.

(This is done internally by making LoS-sized exclusions use LOS_MAX_RANGE
and then dynamically reduce the range of any exclusions which are larger
than you.normal_vision.)

This commit also changes equipment from affecting only you.current_vision
to you.normal_vision. The only gameplay impact is that TSO's halo may be
slightly smaller on a character using LoS-reducers when below 6* piety
(which seems fine to me and arguably even thematically correct).

Note that this change is not fully retroactive. Preexisting exclusions with
a radius smaller than LOS_MAX_RANGE will not be automatically expanded if
one enters Vision form (but they can still be reduced from LoS-)
Remove a left-over statement (Ge0FF)

Allow some more temporary terrain changes to use feat_is_floor()

Expanding them to allow transforming floor-like features that are not
strictly plain, such as decorative floor or food caches.

This affects Primal Wave, Mud Breath, Upheaval and Eruption, hoarfrost
cannons leaving puddles when they die,  Summon Forest tree creation, and
Sigil of Binding.
Actually use the phrase 'jademantle' for the form in-game (Flugkiller)

Adjust vision talisman description for barachi (hellmonk)

To make it more explicit that it doesn't extend their LoS

Weight Ashenzari curse offerings non-equally

By splitting apart all spell skills, but not weapon skills, non-spell
skills became significantly rarer compared to spells than they previously
were.

This commit allows making the weights of given curse offerings non-equal,
and gives melee combat triple normal weight, and spellcasting and fighting
both double.

Tweak Vision form

Remove the -10% HP penalty (which was another element incentivizing people
to switch to jademantle early - since the underskilled HP penalty would
still overtake Vision before reaching 8 skill) and replace it with +1 LoS
and ring-melding.

+1 LoS is thematic, usually considered a mild downside (but also decent
syngery with mystics having 2 means to hit from full LoS at XL 1). Ring
melding won't usually do anything early, but I hope will keep the +LoS from
being overly desireable to latergame archers or full LoS casters.

I'm *slightly* considered about the wider rammifications of this, but I'd
like to test out how this affects the shelf life of this form in the hands
of mystics in particular.

(This commit also fixes an incorrect message for leaving vision form.)

Reduce jademantle effectiveness below minskill

While the crystal HP and direct damage effects of this form were already
quite reduced at low skill, the elemental magic skill bonus was flat. This
combined with the fact that vision already reduced your max HP (which made
the underskill max HP penalty of jademantle easier to swallow) had led to
many people advocating to put the form on almost immediately to help get
Dragon Veins online.

I'm not really happy with advice that involves mostly skipping your
starting form, so this commit now makes the skill bonus and indomitable
healing be reduced below minskill.

Jademantle can still never give you *more* than +2 to your elemental
skills, but shapeshifting below 8 will make it give less. (The amount of
Indomitable you gain at max skill is slightly raised over what it was prior
to this commit, but will also be ~halved at low skill.)

Show actual HP of hypnotail/jade crystals in form table (Monkooky)

Instead of showing a 'percentage HP increase' without indicating what the
base HP actually is until you enter the form and examine them.

This removes the slight automatic randomisation of max HP which previously
happened, but does not otherwise significantly change how durable either of
these things are.

(It does also fix xv lying about the HP of them, too - it would show their
value at minskill, regardless of whether you had more or less skill than
that.)
Remove a leftover debugging statement

Fix a crash with expending an assassin centipede on a multi-attack

Attacking multiple times in one action with the same assassin centipede
that was about to expire (eg: by performing a multi-hit lunge with Wu Jian)
would attempt to perform its destroy fineff twice, and assert on the second
one.

Fix line-join glitches in Russian tutorial

The game joins the lines of a description before showing it
(unwrap_desc in libutil.cc): a line ending in ">" followed by one
starting with "<" is joined with no space, and any other line break
becomes a space. Four line breaks in the Russian files fell foul of
this:

- tutorial2 throwing: "shift-" at the end of a line was shown as
  "[shift- tab]";
- tutorial3 wand_digging: in local tiles the space before the
  alternative was lost and one appeared before the comma;
- tutorial2 compare_monster_desc: a space between the <localtiles>
  and <nomouse> alternatives ended up inside the brackets;
- Dragoncall status: a hyphenated word broken at the hyphen was shown
  with a space in it.

Only line breaks and spaces change; the wording is the same.

Rework randomness in tile difficulties

This has no effect on the distribution or caching, just changing how we
generate the randomness for technical reasons.

Upgrading a save past this commit will do a one-off reroll of the tiles
revealed by passive mapping.

Run RC Lua on a non-seeded RNG

This removes the possibility of predicting or affecting gameplay rolls
using these functions.
Remove duplicate include of state.h from l-crawl.cc

Fix out of bounds index in crawl.bane_description

If the player called crawl.bane_description with an invalid bane name,
it would index an array out of bounds when looking up the description.

Fix out of bounds index in crawl.bane_name

crawl.bane_name gets the full name of a bane from its short name and can
be called by the player with an invalid short name. This would result in
us indexing an array out of bounds when looking up the full name.

Fix crash on demand from crawl.div_rand_round

The player could add a lua function to their RC file that called
crawl.div_rand_round with zero for the divisor. They could then call
this function (e.g. through a macro that calls it when they press a key)
which would result in a crash when dividing by zero.

Fix crash on demand from crawl.random_range

The player could add a lua function to their RC file that called
crawl.random_range with zero or less for the number of rolls parameter.
They could then call this function (e.g. through a macro that calls it
when they press a key) which would trigger an assert and crash their
game.

Interrupt travelling players when their allies gain contam

While the scenario of a player with a lot of zombies autoexploring through
a vault and having them pick up enough contam to explode on you may be
pretty rare, it seems reasonable to stop the player at this point and ask
them what they want to do about it. (Since even aside from hitting you,
they may be in danger of all being destroyed.)

(I considered making allies unwilling to step into these clouds at all, as
they are with blastmotes, but that feels like it would result in odd
effects in some combat scenarios where your zombies would just refuse to
advance on enemies at all; the vaults that use these clouds in battle
situations often use a lot.)

Make peripheral monsters immune to mutagenic clouds

This solves the issue of jademantle crystals picking up contam and
unavoidably exploding on their player while travelling around (but also is
reasonable logic in the first place, I think, since many of these are
transient things).

Fix a crash with mistmane cloud spray against a dead wall monster

The path could only enter the wall so long as the monster there was alive,
so if it died in the attack that was going to trigger cloud spray, beam
setup would crash.

Instead, in cases where there is no beam path, assume that the initial
target is the proper direction.
Remove a superfluous line of code

Add a diviner name; change an Ash knowledge adj.

For the latter, replace Visionary with something else, so that there
is no longer a(n admittedly rare) case where Ashenzari can produce an
artefact named "Visionary Visionary".

Prevent Ely-worshippers from harming neutral monsters

Accidentally getting Ely penance through unexpected means is a recurring
issue. Many effects that target randomly or trigger automatically don't
discern between neutral and hostile monsters, yet hitting a neutral monster
will inflict penance.

There's some argument that it is good flavor to need to be careful around
pacified monsters, but this keeps happening often enough that I have been
persued it might be better to simply prevent the player from doing so,
regardless.

I have some small hesitancies here, as it allows you to pacify a key threat
and then use mass AoE to kill everyone else while leaving them safe, which
feels... slightly negative on both a flavor and mechanical front. But I
feel like the benefits in guaranteeing no accidental penance is probably
worth it.

(One could argue the other good gods could get similar protection, but it
is actually very rare for them to run into neutrals - 95+% of this issue
rests with Ely.)

Note that this does mean that if you somehow end up trapped in a corner
with a pacified monster who insists on trying to kill you, that you still
can't harm them back. Consider it a Vow of Pacifism and find some other
way out.

I am deliberately not extending this protection to friendly monsters since:
a) Very few random effects hit friendlies, but an unknown number don't
   differentiate between hostile and neutral things. So harming friendlies
   is usually an active choice.
b) Being able to use mass AoE while behind friendly creatures is a lot more
   exploitable than it is for pacified ones, and I'm not sure I'm a fan of
   enabling this.

(At some future point, I will do a more careful review of random-targeted
effects and try to reduce the number of them which can hit neutral monsters
also.)

Add actor::hostile()

To match the existing friendly() and neutral() and very slightly shorten
some logic.
Allow dragon veins triggers to maintain East Wind stampede (Flugkiller)

Pull ghost crab claws trigger into do_post_spellcast_effects

At the moment, this mostly means that using dragon veins can trigger it.
Rename urand tile: four_winds -> tranquillity.
Fix spelling.
Fix typos, spelling, wording.

0.35 changelog update (through 74b9271)

Proofread by DracoOmega. We've still got a little bit more to fit into the
version before release, but this should be a good summation of god updates,
unrands, and the Mystic + Stalker additions alongside many other pieces.

Some mostly newer feature tiles

 * A few of the unrands added in e951088 now have new tiles that aren't
   just palette swaps of randart tiles. Their tile sources:
   * Forgewarden's Cuirass: A CC0 piece of armour by idylwild.
   * Hana's Scimitar: roctavian's old randart scimitar and scimitar of
     Flaming Death tiles.
   * "Carina at Dusk": roctavian's current giant spiked club tile
     and dd's old dwarven eveningstar tile.

 * Older Jademantle form tiles accidentally got in during fe7195c, which
   have been replaced here. This flips the pointing directions of fire
   and ice jade crystal charges on both the crystals themselves and the
   fully-charged overlay, and tries to make the ice and earth crystals
   have more visible effects versus the ally crystal rim, all to try and
   help players internalize the jade crystal element alignments. It also
   shifts the octopode tiles from changing body colours into just jutting
   crystals themselves to help with better contrast.

 * To help the fairly staticky electric effects added in 733b4dd stand
   out better against lighter backgrounds, I have edited the stronger
   electric bolt effects to be slightly smaller but fit on some exterior
   outlining- this does make them a bit closer to the weaker shots, but
   being both larger and brighter should distinguish them regardless.
   (The previous graphics have been preserved for Plasma Beam alone,
   since it already looks fine with that one stacking a brighter and
   darker effect together.)

 * With the new Mystic and talisman additions getting randart versions
   added to the rltiles/UNUSED folders, I have also added a lupine
   randart talisman tile I made some months ago to the same list,
   mixing together LemurRobot's claw mutation tiles with his previous
   edit of Sastreii's beast talismans meant for beast talisman randarts.
   We're still fairly far off from having a complete set, but it should
   be good for future contributors to not accidentally submit something
   already covered for.

Bullish mutation icons (carf)

With some slight colour modifications, this adds minotaur headbutt
retaliation and stage 1/2 hooves mutation tiles by carf, appreciated
for making aking more progress on a few of the many old Art Requests
entries. This also adds carf to the credits list.

Rework the Russian tutorial

ru/tutorial.txt had 57 of the English file's 88 entries, and more than
half of those were defective, so the file is retranslated against the
current English rather than patched.

The worst problem was English left inside <input> tags. Those are shown
to the player verbatim in brackets, so a Russian tutorial was telling
beginners to press [arrow keys] and [left click]. Some instructions
were also stale: tutorial1 downstairs said Shift-Click where the
English has said left click for some time, and tutorial1 levelmap had
a sentence that stopped mid-clause and used <console> where the English
uses <nomouse>.

Key names that are printed on keyboards - Space, Enter, Escape, Shift,
Numlock, Tab - stay in Latin, while descriptions of actions are
translated. $cmd[] references are untouched, and the two :nowrap key
diagrams keep their layout character for character.

Markup now matches the English in all 88 entries.

Add a hostile check to crab claws (tekkud)

Don't spawn additional clouds from beating up your own spectrals.

Marshall monsterinfo spells (KleptoBismol)

This stops us forgetting ghost and panlord spell sets on reload.

Add passives to you lua module

This exposes the list of passives (as shown on %) to user lua. We do
this as a table not a comma-separated string like statuses, both because
that's what it is and because one of the passives has a comma in it.

Fix item menu not changing operation

Since 1919f11, changing the operation while in an item menu did not
change the operation attempted. This meant that you could not read after
switching from the quaff menu, and you could remove gear you were not
wearing (causing a crash).

Also close a little hole where we checked the legality of the operation
too early, e.g. allowing the player to wear things while berserk if they
got there via a different operation.

This was always intended behaviour, but apparently MID_YOU_FAULTLESS
doesn't work for this purpose if set_agent(you) is used earlier to set the
killer_type.

Possible some other uses of that should be reexamined, but there is now an
even more convenient way to flag a beam not to blame the player for things,
so use that instead here for now.

Update force_more for new Ash flavour (acrobat).

Whoops...

Fixes #5488
Fix Jade Mantle skill enhancement message

Remove now-redundant holiness checks (DracoOmega)

Since monsters with undead and non-living holiness get poison immunity
from that.

Fix check for darts&poison immunity (DracoOmega).

Closes #5491.
Fix spacing.

Adjust Gnoll Weapons, Shapeshifting, and Invocations Aptitudes Upward +1

In response to commit 0a2c1f0 in master, which reduced Gnoll spell
aptitudes by 1 to encourage broader use of tools, this change boosts
several non-spell aptitudes with the same goal.

Increasing weapon aptitudes by 1 allows Gnolls to reach respectable
usability across all weapon types by late Lair to late Dungeon (for
example, minimum delay on tier-1 fast weapons and 1.0 delay on a broad
axe). This brings the melee progression closer to the spell progression
available to the Gnoll at the same stage, while keeping it slightly
slower than Humans.

Increasing Shapeshifting by 1 should encourage greater use of talismans.
In conjunction with the previous commit, this puts the Shapeshifter
background closer to the progression of other species: the Protean Talisman
becomes available around D4, rather than immediately on turn 1, yet
encourages more use later in the game as the skill keeps up with the
difficulty curve.

The +1 Invocations aptitude, together with the reduced synergy between
talismans and the top Gnoll god (Ash), may encourage greater
experimentation with other gods, particually with the recent changes to
Ash.

[Committer's note: very slightly edited commit message]

Pull some gnoll xp into manuals

To further adjust gnoll power curve without gutting their apts or stats
even more, this commit pulls 50% of gnoll starting xp into a manual for
each skill. This makes them significantly weaker on D:1, but improve at
their class skills faster for a little while at the beginning of the game,
before reaching parity.

The time it takes to recover the "missing" xp depends on the skill value;
lower skills catch up faster than higher ones. For example, a GnCj will
finish their stealth manual about halfway through xl 7 but needs to get to
high xl 10 to finish the conjurations manual. This also means that "hybrid"
starts with many starting skills will catch up faster than starts with only
a few skills. Even with this change, gnoll should start with more skill
than the equivalent human background across all backgrounds in the game.

In making this, I tested the following values with gncj against trunk apts,
which I have preserved here for posterity:
Unmodified gncj: 4.4 dodge, 4.0 stealth, 4.4 spc, 6.4 conj
25% xp in manual: 3.7 dodge, 3.4 stealth, 3.7 spc, 5.4 conj
1/3 xp in manual: 3.5 dodge, 3.2 stealth, 3.5 spc, 5.1 conj
50% xp in manual: 3.0 dodge, 2.7 stealth, 3.0 spc, 4.3 conj

Tweak some (arguably) vestigial Ashenzari flavour

While cursed item are core to Ashenzari's gameplay loop, them being called
simply 'cursed' (and having such a plain message for accepting this curse
as 'your +0 robe glows black for a moment') is a legacy of cursed items
once being a widespread thing in Crawl. Ash was interesting at the time for
giving an *upside* to a property that was normally purely a *downside* (and
recontextualizing scrolls), but now when the only cursed items in the game
are intrinsically divinely-associated (and almost purely positive!), I feel
we can do a little better.

This commit adjusts a bunch of flavour messages to lean into what is
suggested by both Ashenzari's description and the 'Shatter the Chains'
ability name, giving what is hopefully some slightly more evocative flavour
to performing these rituals. Items are referred to individually as 'bound'
to the player, rather than cursed (though a 'divine curse' is mentioned in
a few places).

(I have not exhaustively renamed every function or flag in the codebase
that calls these 'cursed' - at least in part because that is less ambiguous
in code than 'bound'.)

There is no functional change here, to be clear.

Make Ash curse skill enhancements more concise

With most curses boosting a single skill now, it's both verbose and kind
of weird to list them all in duplicate (eg: "Summonings: Summonings").
Just combine all the curses into one line.

Split apart the Devices curse into Evocations and Shapeshifting

While it's true that the way curses work at the moment makes Shapeshifting
more niche on Ash characters, it feels awkward to me that two extremely
unrelated skills are bundled together now that we no longer bundle anything
except closely-related skills. (Especially under a category like 'devices'.
Do talismans feels like 'using a device'? They don't to me.)

If Shapeshifting ends up feeling like too much of a dud in a way that
negatively affects the god's power level, I'd rather consider addressing
that in some other way.

Split up Ash curses

New spells have made curse skill sets like elements, which were once likely to
have utility only for one of the boosted skills, extremely relevant for
multiple skills at once (by doubly boosting hellfire mortar, for example). In
order to future-proof against that, and to somewhat reduce Ashenzari's total
skill bonus at endgame, most curse types will now boost a single skill but
will be offered in sets of three rather than two. The melee weapon and
ranged curses are unchanged since those skills are mostly redundant with one
another. Devices is also unchanged since shapeshifting is relatively niche
with Ashenzari.

Prevent form XP tracking writing out of bounds

Form XP tracking could write beyond the end of you.xp_by_form for
max-XL characters, in the multi-XL-gain loop. Add a conditional to
prevent this, analogous to the one in level_change().

Fix a crash when aiming Rimeblight at a wall (rypofalem)

The targeter tries to find the last-hit space on the beam's path, but
since 16ceb2c it became possible to have a 0-length path , meaning it would
check a position corresponding to random junk data insted (potentially
crashing).

Make the player actually require the claimed 10 XP for XL 2, instead of 9

This will no doubt have profound balance consequences.

(Honestly, the off-by-one is so odd here that I couldn't help but wonder if
there was some deliberate reason for it, but I don't see it.)

Add tracking for percentage of each XL spent in a given form

This adds a new section to the chardump (and the required internal
tracking) showing what percentage of each XL's XP was gained while in a
different form.

(This tracks based on your *default* form, so polymorph and !lig still
count as whatever you would be outside of those effects.)

At the end of this section, it totals how many XLs had 95% or more of their
XP gained in a given form (implying the player was in it basically
continuously).

This is useful statistical information and there's potential to do more
with it in future - for instance, handing out form-related titles only if
the player actually spends all XL past a certain level in a form, rather
than just being able to swap to it at the end. There is maybe potential
for future conducts using this information as well?

This isn't in a form that can be queried by Sequell at the moment, since I
wasn't sure the best way to go about that. But with the information being
tracked, it would be easier to add this in future, should we choose to.

Don't do knockback from reflected stars

Fixes #5466

Stop foxfires and stars from hitting themselves

When reflected by the warlock's mirror, we would get messages like "the
foxfire hits the foxfire". We fix this by killing the monsters before
firing the beams; this works because cleanup is deferred, so we can
still read the monster's name etc for beam properties.

fix: gecko tail related constriction crash

Clear the player from the monster's constricted list when the player
loses their tail.
fix: leftover print statement

Adjust Foul Shadow mutation description

To display properly in 80x24 console.
Redraw MP on Dragon Vein activation
Document Dragon Vein's MP cost on activation

Fix debug builds crashing on startup

Caused by 49c5af30d7, selecting a background with a spell in its quiver
was returning early and trying to generate an invalid ray.

Fix large rock desc species check.

It now consistently refers to Oni instead of the obsolete Ogres, and no
longer refers to Formicids' obsolete ability to throw large rocks.

Update it in all the translations as well (even though only the Russian
and Chinese translations have been updated enough to even mention Oni in
species.txt instead of Ogres, and the French translation of items.txt
is so old it used a check that would cover Ogre-Magi).

Maybe there should be a Lua binding for you.can_throw_large_rocks(), and
items.txt and all its translations should just use that? At least this
works for the time being.
